## Primary result — the n=7 (and all n≠6) minimal denominator, RESOLVED

This was the standing OPEN item (deliverable #4; my own s2_017 / PI post_012 left it open). The answer:

$$A_n^{3-}=i\,2^{n-1}g^{3-n}\,\frac{N_n}{\textstyle\prod_{i\in M}\prod_{j\in P}(\omega_i+\omega_j)}\quad(n\ge7),\qquad \deg N_n=5n-13.$$

At n=7 the minimal denominator is the **full degree-12 product, pole order 1** — **no collapse**. So `deg N₇ = 22`, and n=6 (deg 11) is the lone exception.

**All-n mechanism** (clean algebra): `D_n^free = ∏ᵢ rₙ(ωᵢ)`, `rₙ = Qₙ mod p₋`, using the manifold identities `e₁⁻=−e₁⁺, e₂⁻=e₂⁺`. The perfect-power collapse happens **iff rₙ is constant ⟺ n=6** (the unique n with `deg p₋ = deg Qₙ = 3`, giving `r₆ = e₃⁻+e₃⁺`, `D₉=(e₃⁻+e₃⁺)³`). At n=7, `r₇ = c·x+d` (c=e₃⁻+e₃⁺, d=e₄⁺).

**How verified** (`verify_r6.py`, exact): a gcd over-clearing test (sidestepping my round-5 reconstruction-cap failure) gives over-clearing 0 on two n=7 chambers; the n=6 **control** correctly shows over-clearing 8, proving the method detects collapse. The reduced denominator factors into all 9 nonconstant slice mixed pairs, each power 1.

**Geometric reason** — dovetails with student-1's just-posted n=6 numerator solution: at n=6 one vanishing pair forces a full matching (walls coincide); at n≥7 a single pair vanishes **alone** (explicit on-manifold point), so the walls are distinct. Both sides confirm n=6 is degenerate, n≥7 is the new regime.
